newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares nudge up at close in thin volume.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares nudge up at close in thin volume.

text.p: Bombay share prices ended in positive territory on Friday in sluggish weekend trade and brokers said they were keeping their fingers crossed.
"The market will run out of steam if expectations do not materialise," said broker Sunil Kothari.
He said shares were driven by speculators who were anticipating changes in a controversial tax proposal before it becomes law next month.
The 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index closed 19.73 points higher at a provisional 3,513.34 after falling to 3,489.75 in early trade.
The 500-stock CRISIL index slipped 0.3 points to a provisional 696.78.
The 50-stock NSE index gained 2.68 points, or 0.26 percent, to a provisional 1,028.68.
Trading on the National bourse was lacklustre.
"We hardly got any business today," said Cyrus Rastomjee, dealer at brokerage El Dorado Guarantee. "Very dull."

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram will address parliament on Monday about the proposed 1996/97 (April-March) budget, but any amendments to tax proposals would have to wait until September 9 or 10, a ministry official said in Delhi.
Buying by foreign funds drove TELCO up 11.50 rupees to 509.75 and Bajaj Auto 6.50 to 1,058.50, traders said.
East India Hotels dropped 13 rupees to 647 and Indian Hotels 15.25 to 770.
Hindalco rose 9.0 rupees to 1,015.25, SBI 2.50 to 271.75, BSES 2.25 to 196.75, MTNL 3.75 to 207.75, Gujarat Ambuja Cement 2.50 to 324.50 and TISCO 0.50 to 195.50.
Hind Lever shed 8.25 rupees to 841.75, Grasim 5.25 to 442.25, ACC 2.75 to 2,157 and Colgate 3.25 to 259.50.
Activity was also hit by the last day of weekly account on the BSE, traders said.
